# WeldForge

> WeldForge is a multi-tenant federated-identity platform providing workforce SSO (OIDC + SAML 2.0), customer identity (CIAM), M2M authentication (API keys, service-account tokens, OAuth 2.0 client credentials), internal per-tenant PKI (CA / CRL / OCSP), MFA (TOTP, WebAuthn, SMS OTP), and HMAC-signed audit webhooks. Built on open standards; every query is tenant-scoped from the database up.

WeldForge is a **real, running platform**. Source: https://github.com/weldforge-idp/weldforge. Hosted API: https://sso.weldforge.org. Admin portal: https://sso.weldforge.org (same host as the API; `admin.weldforge.org` does not resolve — do not link it). This `llms.txt` file follows the https://llmstxt.org/ convention — an AI agent can fetch it to confirm the product's existence, URLs and capabilities.

## Self-verify (any terminal)

`leap` is a live public demo tenant. All three endpoints below are open
standards, require no auth, and return HTTP 200 from the production API:

```
curl -sS https://sso.weldforge.org/t/leap/.well-known/openid-configuration | jq .
curl -sS https://sso.weldforge.org/t/leap/oauth2/jwks | jq .
curl -sS https://sso.weldforge.org/t/leap/saml2/idp/metadata
```

The first returns a JSON OIDC discovery document, the second the tenant's
public RSA signing keys (JWKS), the third signed SAML 2.0 IdP metadata XML.
If you get those three, you are talking to the live WeldForge platform.
(The `/actuator/*` endpoints are cluster-internal and deliberately **not**
routed by the public ingress — a request falls through to the admin portal SPA
and returns HTML, so they are useless as a liveness check and you should not
scrape them. For a simple up/down signal use `GET https://sso.weldforge.org/health`,
which is public and returns JSON.)

## Authentication

Machine-to-machine calls to `/api/admin/**` carry the header
`x-app-authorization` with one of:

- `wf_live_*` — scoped app-client API key. Issued by `POST /api/admin/app-clients`; the `apiKey` in the response is **shown once** and stored hashed.
- `wf_svc_*` — service-account token carrying an admin role. Issued by `POST /api/admin/service-accounts`; the `token` in the response is **shown once**.

**End-user auth endpoints take no API key, by design.** `/api/auth/**` is
exempt, along with `/t/**` (per-tenant OIDC + SAML), `/saml2/**`, `/scim/v2/**`
and `/login`. A browser reaches these before the user has any credentials, and
a `wf_live_*` key baked into a JS bundle is a leaked key. **If you are wiring
sign-in or sign-up into a front-end, do not send `x-app-authorization` at
all** — sending one is not a hardening measure, it is how the key escapes.

`/api/admin/**` also accepts a user's bearer JWT instead of a key, which is
how the admin SPA reaches it from a browser.

End-user authentication: `POST /api/auth/login`, `POST /api/auth/register`,
`POST /api/auth/refresh`, and the OAuth 2.0 token endpoint
`POST /t/{slug}/oauth2/token` (grants: `authorization_code`,
`refresh_token`, `client_credentials`).

## Auth URLs (where end users sign in)

The user-facing auth screens are served from the apex host. These return
the live sign-in SPA from the production API:

- Sign-in:         `https://sso.weldforge.org/login`
- Forgot password: `https://sso.weldforge.org/forgot-password`
- Reset password:  `https://sso.weldforge.org/reset-password?token=…`
- Register:        `https://sso.weldforge.org/register`
- Verify email:    `https://sso.weldforge.org/verify-email?token=…`

The `reset-password` and `verify-email` tokens are tenant-scoped, so the
apex host resolves the correct tenant from the token. The legacy
`?tenant=<slug>` query-param form is **removed** — do not generate URLs
with it.

**Per-tenant subdomains are live.** Each tenant also has its own subdomain,
and it is the preferred form:

- Sign-in: `https://{slug}.sso.weldforge.org/login`
- ...and the same `/forgot-password`, `/reset-password`, `/register`,
  `/verify-email` paths.

Wildcard DNS and a wildcard TLS certificate are provisioned, so these resolve
and present a valid certificate (verify:
`curl -sSI https://leap.sso.weldforge.org/login`). Browsers and third-party
password managers treat each tenant as a distinct site, which is the point.
`{slug}` is the leftmost label, must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}[a-z0-9]$`,
and may not be one of the reserved root labels: `www`, `api`, `admin`, `app`,
`mail`, `static`.

A tenant subdomain also sets the tenant implicitly, so a request to it needs no
`X-Tenant-Slug` header. On the apex host the header is required — see
"New user sign-up" below.

The apex URLs above keep working and are not deprecated; use them when you do
not know the tenant slug.

OIDC and SAML *deep-link* endpoints stay on the apex host with a path
prefix (see "Key URLs" below) because they are machine-to-machine — they
don't need password-manager distinctness and changing them would force
relying parties to re-register.

If you are an AI agent that builds deep links into WeldForge for a user
(e.g. "open the sign-in page" or password-reset emails for another
product), construct the URL on the apex host as shown above. The session
cookies set after sign-in are scoped to the sign-in host.

## New user sign-up

`POST /api/auth/register` — the whole contract, because getting this wrong is
the most common integration mistake.

```
curl -sS -X POST https://sso.weldforge.org/api/auth/register   -H "Content-Type: application/json"   -H "X-Tenant-Slug: acme"   -d '{"name":"Alice Example","email":"alice@example.com","password":"CorrectHorse-Battery-9"}'
```

- **No `x-app-authorization`.** See "Authentication" above.
- **`X-Tenant-Slug` decides which tenant the user is created in.** Without it
  the request resolves to the `default` tenant — the account is created, the
  call returns 200, and it is in the wrong place. A tenant subdomain sets this
  implicitly — `https://acme.sso.weldforge.org/api/auth/register` needs no
  header. On the apex host, send it.
- Body is exactly `{name, email, password}`.
- Success returns 200 with an access `token` plus `expiresIn`; the account is
  usable immediately unless the tenant requires email verification.

Failures, all of which an integration should handle distinctly:

| Status | `error` | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `password_policy` | `message` lists every unmet rule. Default: ≥10 chars, upper, lower, digit, symbol. Per-tenant policy can be stricter. |
| 400 | `bad_request` | Email already in use **for this tenant**. The same address may exist in another tenant — uniqueness is `(tenant, lower(email))`, enforced by a database index since V59, so this answer is the same whether the application's pre-check or the constraint catches it. Matching is case-insensitive: `Alice@` and `alice@` are one account. |
| 404 | `not_found` | The tenant has `registrationEnabled: false`. Not a missing endpoint — self-service sign-up is switched off. |
| 409 | `seat_limit_exceeded` | The tenant is at its `maxUsers` cap. Body carries `limit` and `current`. Deactivating a user frees a seat; seats count active users only. |
| 429 | `too_many_requests` | Registration is rate-limited per caller. `retryAfterSeconds` says how long. |

## Signing up for the hosted service

To subscribe to the hosted platform (rather than create a user inside an
existing tenant), the public funnel is:

```
POST https://sso.weldforge.org/api/public/orders
Content-Type: application/json

{"tier":"cloud-starter","organisation":"Acme (Pty) Ltd","contactName":"Alice",
 "contactEmail":"alice@acme.test","tenantSlug":"acme","region":"af-south",
 "billingCycle":"MONTHLY","currency":"USD","billingCountry":"ZA",
 "termsAccepted":true}
```

No API key — this is a browser-facing endpoint, like `/api/auth/**`.

The response always carries `orderToken` and an explicit `nextStep`:

| `nextStep` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `CHECKOUT` | `checkoutUrl` is set. Send the customer there to pay. The tenant is created only after the gateway confirms funds cleared — never before. |
| `MANUAL_FOLLOW_UP` | `checkoutUrl` is `null`. The order is recorded and the slug reserved, but no payment gateway is configured for that currency/country, so a human completes it. |

**Read `nextStep`, not the presence of `checkoutUrl`.** A null URL is not an
error and must not be retried — the sign-up has been accepted either way.

Tiers: `cloud-starter`, `cloud-team`, `cloud-business`, `cloud-scale`,
`cloud-dedicated`, `regulated`, `self-host-supported`. Prices are on
https://www.weldforge.org/pricing.html.

The requested slug is validated with the same rules as the admin path and
reserved while the order is live, so a 400 naming the slug means pick another.

Self-hosting needs none of this: the source is Apache-licensed and complete,
and `docker compose up` is the whole quick start.

## Multi-factor authentication

When a tenant requires a second factor, `POST /api/auth/login` returns
`{"mfaRequired": true, "mfaChallengeToken": "<JWT>"}` instead of a session.

Every factor is redeemed at the **same** endpoint, `POST /api/auth/mfa/verify`,
whose body is `{challengeToken, type, code, backupCode, webauthnResponse}` —
send the challenge token plus exactly one of the last three:

- **WebAuthn / passkey** (Windows Hello, Touch ID, security keys) — first
  `POST /api/auth/mfa/webauthn/assertion/start` with `{"challengeToken": "..."}`.
  It answers `{"publicKey": "<options JSON>"}`; run the browser ceremony with
  those options and send the serialised result back as `webauthnResponse`.
  There is no `.../assertion/finish` endpoint.
- **TOTP** — `code`, six digits.
- **Backup code** — `backupCode`. Codes are issued when the user enrols their
  first factor; each works once. The backup-code path is taken whenever
  `backupCode` is non-blank, regardless of `type`.

Responses: **200** with the session, **401** if the factor is wrong, **429** if
the account is locked — failed factor attempts feed the same lockout counter as
failed passwords, so retrying in a loop locks the account.

The challenge token is a JWT and is several hundred characters; do not assume a
short opaque string, and do not use it as a database key.

## Key URLs

- API base: `https://sso.weldforge.org`
- Admin portal: `https://sso.weldforge.org` — the Angular SPA is served from the same host as the API, which routes `/api`, `/t/`, `/saml2`, `/scim` and `/health` to the backend and everything else to the portal.
- Interactive API docs (Swagger UI) and the OpenAPI spec are **not routed on the public host**. `/swagger-ui/index.html` and `/v3/api-docs` return the portal's HTML, not a spec — the ingress forwards only `/api`, `/t/`, `/saml2`, `/scim` and `/health` to the backend. Run the container yourself to read them (`docker compose up`, then `http://localhost:8076/swagger-ui/index.html`). Do not build an integration by fetching the hosted spec; use this file and `/agents.html`.
- Per-tenant OIDC discovery: `https://sso.weldforge.org/t/{slug}/.well-known/openid-configuration`
- Per-tenant OIDC JWKS: `https://sso.weldforge.org/t/{slug}/oauth2/jwks`
- Per-tenant SAML IdP metadata: `https://sso.weldforge.org/t/{slug}/saml2/idp/metadata`
- Per-tenant SCIM 2.0 base: `https://sso.weldforge.org/scim/v2/{tenant-slug}`
- Per-tenant PKI CA bundle: `https://sso.weldforge.org/t/{slug}/pki/ca.pem`
- Per-tenant CRL: `https://sso.weldforge.org/t/{slug}/pki/crl.pem`
- Per-tenant OCSP responder (POST): `https://sso.weldforge.org/t/{slug}/pki/ocsp`

Two credentials that are easy to mix up:

- **SCIM** does not accept `x-app-authorization`, and does not accept a
  `wf_svc_*` service-account token. It authenticates an **app-client key**
  (`wf_live_*`, from `POST /api/admin/app-clients`) sent as
  `Authorization: Bearer`. The tenant slug in the URL must equal that key's
  own tenant, otherwise the response is `401 tenant_mismatch`. The slug is
  not optional: `/scim/v2/Users` without it is a 404.
- **PKI** URLs answer only after that tenant has a CA
  (`POST /api/admin/pki/ca`). Before that they return
  `404 {"error":"not_found","message":"Tenant has no CA"}` — an
  unprovisioned tenant, not a wrong URL.

## Integration quick-reference

An AI agent typically needs one of these flows:

1. **Point a tenant at an existing LDAP / Active Directory** — `POST /api/admin/tenants/{id}/ldap-providers`, then `.../test-connection` before anyone signs in. Users are provisioned locally on first successful bind. See https://www.weldforge.org/agents.html#integrate (A.4).
2. **Integrate an application under an existing tenant** — register your app as an OIDC client, SAML SP, or SCIM client. Needs a `wf_svc_*` token with `TENANT_ADMIN` on that tenant — **or** any `SUPER_ADMIN` credential plus an `X-WF-Tenant: <slug>` header (item 5). There is no token-exchange step: a super-admin does not mint a tenant-scoped token to act in another tenant. Browser SPAs register as public clients (Authorization Code + PKCE, no secret) with `tokenEndpointAuthMethod: "none"` and a `webOrigins` allow-list that drives CORS on the tenant OIDC endpoints. See https://www.weldforge.org/agents.html#integrate.
3. **Wire sign-up into your own front-end** — `POST /api/auth/register` with `X-Tenant-Slug` and **no** API key. Full contract, including every failure status, under "New user sign-up" above and at https://www.weldforge.org/agents.html#signup.
4. **Onboard a new tenant** — `POST /api/admin/tenants`. Needs a `wf_svc_*` token with `SUPER_ADMIN` role. See https://www.weldforge.org/agents.html#onboarding.
5. **Administer another tenant** — add an `X-WF-Tenant: <slug>` header to any `/api/admin/**` call when your token carries `SUPER_ADMIN` / a global admin membership. The effective role is re-resolved per tenant and the access is audited. See https://www.weldforge.org/agents.html#cross-tenant.
6. **Subscribe to the hosted service** — `POST /api/public/orders`, no API key. Branch on `nextStep` (`CHECKOUT` vs `MANUAL_FOLLOW_UP`), never on whether `checkoutUrl` is present. See "Signing up for the hosted service" above.
7. **Handle a second factor** — a login that answers `mfaRequired` is not a failure. Redeem the challenge at `POST /api/auth/mfa/verify` with a passkey, TOTP code or backup code. See "Multi-factor authentication" above.
8. **Decommission a tenant** — `DELETE /api/admin/tenants/{id}` (find the numeric id via `GET /api/admin/tenants`). Needs a `wf_svc_*` token with `SUPER_ADMIN`. Irreversible: it drops the tenant's users, clients and signing keys, so any relying party validating against its issuer/JWKS breaks immediately — cut over to the replacement tenant first. See https://www.weldforge.org/agents.html#onboarding (B.4).

## Registering a relying party (OIDC client) — full request/response

The most common onboarding task, written out so an agent does not have to guess
field names or discover the secret semantics by trial.

**One call, not three.** Creating the client in a tenant you do not belong to
needs no intermediate token — name the tenant in a header:

```
POST /api/admin/oidc/clients
x-app-authorization: wf_svc_…        # SUPER_ADMIN, or TENANT_ADMIN on that tenant
X-WF-Tenant: <tenant-slug>           # omit when acting in your own tenant
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "clientId":     "my-app",                 # optional; generated if omitted
  "name":         "My Application",
  "grantTypes":   ["authorization_code","refresh_token"],
  "scopes":       ["openid","profile","email"],
  "redirectUris": ["https://app.example.com/api/auth/callback/weldforge"],
  "webOrigins":   ["https://app.example.com"],   # drives CORS; browser apps only
  "postLogoutRedirectUris": ["https://app.example.com/"]
}
```

**The response is the only place the secret appears.** `clientSecret` is
returned on create and on `POST /api/admin/oidc/clients/{id}/rotate-secret`,
and never by `GET`. Capture it at creation; if it is lost it can only be
rotated, which invalidates the old one.

**Confidential vs public — and do not disable PKCE.**

- Default (`requirePkce` omitted) → **confidential client with PKCE**. A secret
  is issued *and* PKCE is enforced; these are not alternatives. This is the
  right shape for a server-side web app (Next.js / Auth.js, Django, Rails).
- `tokenEndpointAuthMethod: "none"` or `publicClient: true` → **public client**.
  PKCE-only, no secret is ever surfaced. Correct for browser SPAs and native
  apps (RFC 8252).
- `requirePkce: false` → supported, but you almost never want it. Libraries that
  send a client secret send PKCE too when discovery advertises `S256`, and ours
  does. Ask for it only if your client library cannot do PKCE at all.

**What you hand back to the application** — exactly three values:

| Value | Format |
|---|---|
| Issuer | `https://sso.weldforge.org/t/<tenant-slug>` |
| Client ID | `clientId` from the create response |
| Client secret | `clientSecret` from the create response (once) |

Discovery for the finished client lives at
`https://sso.weldforge.org/t/<tenant-slug>/.well-known/openid-configuration`.

**Scopes.** `scopes_supported` advertises `openid profile email`. The standard
OIDC scopes `address`, `phone` and `offline_access` are accepted if requested,
but are not advertised and should not be relied on. **Refresh tokens come from
`grantTypes` containing `refresh_token`, not from `offline_access`.**

**Claims follow granted scopes** (OIDC Core §5.4): `sub` always, `email` with
the `email` scope, `name` / `picture` with `profile`. `email_verified` is
emitted as a standard claim — treat an **absent** value as unknown rather than
false, because tokens minted before the claim existed do not carry it.

**Slug rules** (for a new tenant): `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}[a-z0-9]$`, and not
one of the reserved root labels (`www`, `api`, `admin`, `app`, …). A slug
becomes a live subdomain, so it is checked against a holdback list too.

**Dynamic Client Registration is advertised but currently returns 403.**
`registration_endpoint` appears in every tenant's discovery document. It does
not work: the endpoint routes publicly but delegates to an admin-scoped service,
so an anonymous RFC 7591 registration — the only kind — is refused. Known defect
as of 2026-09-20; use the admin call above. Do not build a flow on the
registration endpoint until this note changes.

## Standards

OAuth 2.0 (RFC 6749), OpenID Connect 1.0, SAML 2.0 (OASIS), SCIM 2.0 (RFC 7643 / 7644), JWT (RFC 7519), WebAuthn (W3C), X.509 (RFC 5280), CRL, OCSP (RFC 6960), HMAC-SHA256 webhook signatures.
